description: Every published Sterling component. `figma` lists the properties as the Figma library names them; `react` lists the coded component's props, each with the Figma property it stands for. Figma names are sentence case and map one to one to camelCase props (Show icon ↔ showIcon). Code has no `state` prop: hover, pressed, and focus are CSS, and the rest are props (see each component's `states`). `related` points into guidelines.json.

components.name: Controls/Button
components.description: Triggers an action, in primary, secondary, ghost, or danger style.
components.details: Kind × Size × State (default / hover / pressed / focus / disabled). Label, Show icon, and Icon are component properties. Height and padding follow the Density mode. Danger uses status/critical, never finance/sell.
components.useWhen: Triggering an action. One primary per area; secondary for alternatives; ghost in dense toolbars and bulk bars; danger for destructive actions.
components.dontUseWhen: Navigating to another page (use a link), toggling a setting (use a checkbox), or Buy/Sell trade actions styled with danger.

components.name: Controls/Icon button
components.description: A square, icon-only button for well-known actions in dense rows and toolbars.
components.details: Kind (secondary / ghost / danger) × Size (sm / md) × State (default / hover / pressed / focus / disabled). Square, sized to the control height (Density). Icon is an instance swap; Label is the accessible name — its layer is hidden, so set it to the action ("Delete row") and use it as aria-label and tooltip in code. Danger uses status/critical.
components.useWhen: A well-known action in a dense row or toolbar (more, delete, edit, refresh), with a tooltip.
components.dontUseWhen: The action isn't obvious from the icon (use Controls/Button with a label), or it's the main action of the area.

components.name: Controls/Link
components.description: An always-underlined text link for navigation and for shortcuts such as applying a filter.
components.details: Inline text link. Size (sm = Label 12 / md = Body 13) × State (default / hover / focus). Label is a text property. Always underlined in accent/default (accent/hover on hover), so it never relies on color alone; focus adds the outside ring.
components.useWhen: Navigating, or applying a shortcut such as a filter ("Filter: Status is Exception"), from within text or a summary panel.
components.dontUseWhen: The action changes data (use Controls/Button), or it's the main action of an area.

components.name: Controls/Checkbox
components.description: Selects rows or options, with off, on, and indeterminate values.
components.details: Checked (off / on / indeterminate) × State (default / hover / focus / disabled). Checked states use accent/default with a text/inverse glyph; focus adds a focus/ring outline. Label and Show label (off by default) add a visible label for use outside the grid; in a grid row the row itself labels the checkbox.
components.useWhen: Selecting rows or items for a bulk action, or choosing any number of options (turn Show label on outside the grid).
components.dontUseWhen: The choice applies immediately like an on/off setting (use a switch), or only one option can be chosen (use a radio or select).

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.note: Reports the value the user chose as "on" or "off"; Figma has no behavior.

components.name: Chip/Status
components.description: Shows a record's status with a tone color, an icon, and a short label.
components.details: Tone (positive / warning / critical / info / neutral) with a tone-specific icon. Label and Show icon are component properties; labels longer than 160px truncate. Colors: status/<tone>-subtle background, status/<tone>-strong text and icon.
components.useWhen: Showing the status of a record (in a grid cell, card, or header). Keep labels to one or two words.
components.dontUseWhen: The status is an applied filter (use Chip/Filter), or the chip would be the only signal — keep the icon or label visible.

components.name: Chip/Side
components.description: Shows the buy or sell side of an order or trade.
components.details: Side (buy / sell) of an order or trade. The label carries the meaning; override it with B / S in tight columns. Colors: finance/<side>-subtle background, finance/<side>-strong text.
components.useWhen: Showing the side of an order, trade, or position in a grid cell or ticket header (swap a Type = chip cell's Chip to this).
components.dontUseWhen: Showing gain or loss (use a gain / loss cell), or as a Buy / Sell action (use Controls/Button).

props.name: label
props.note: "Buy" or "Sell" by default. In Figma, a text layer to override (for example with B / S).

components.name: Chip/Filter
components.description: Shows one applied filter, with a control to remove it.
components.details: Applied filter, State (default / hover / pressed / focus). Label and Show remove are component properties; labels longer than 240px truncate. Height follows Density → control/height-sm.
components.useWhen: Summarizing filters already applied to a view, with a way to remove each one.
components.dontUseWhen: Showing a record's status (use Chip/Status), or offering filters to apply (use inputs and selects in a filters panel).

props.name: onRemove
props.note: Called when the chip is used to remove its filter; Figma has no behavior.

components.name: Grid/HeaderCell
components.description: Labels a grid column, with optional sorting and left or right alignment.
components.details: Sort (none / asc / desc) × Align (left / right) × State (default / hover / focus). Label and Show sort are component properties. Only a sorted header (asc / desc) shows its icon at rest; an unsorted one reveals ⇕ on hover and focus, so a grid shows at most one sort icon. Show sort off means the column can't be sorted. The sort icon belongs next to its label, and a right-aligned label stays flush with the numbers. In this component the label fills the cell and truncates at its width, so the icon sits at the cell edge: size numeric columns to their values and it lands beside the label. Height follows Density → row/height.
components.useWhen: Labeling a grid column; use Align = right for numeric columns so headers line up with the numbers.
components.dontUseWhen: The column can't be sorted — turn Show sort off rather than using a different header.

props.name: onSort
props.note: Called when the person asks to sort by the column; Figma has no behavior.

components.name: Grid/BodyCell
components.description: One grid cell for text, numbers, gain or loss, a chip, or a checkbox, in every row and validation state.
components.details: Type (text / numeric / gain / loss / chip / checkbox) × State (default / hover / selected / selected-hover / focus / warning / warning-focus / error / error-focus). Numeric, gain and loss cells are right-aligned in the Numeric style and never truncate (size the column instead); text values truncate. Gain and loss add ▲ / ▼ and finance/gain / loss — type the sign in Value (+1.25%, −0.80%). Warning and error add a border and an icon, so they never rely on color alone, and a flagged cell keeps its look while its row is hovered or selected. Focus variants are for future editable cells; read-only grids show focus on header buttons and row checkboxes only. Chip and Checkbox are exposed nested instances; swap the Chip to Chip/Side for buy / sell.
components.useWhen: Building custom rows or tables from individual cells, or overriding one cell's state (e.g. a value that breaks a rule).
components.dontUseWhen: You need a whole row — use Grid/Row, which keeps cell widths and states consistent.

props.name: children
props.note: The StatusChip or Checkbox of a chip or checkbox cell. In Figma it is an exposed nested instance.

components.name: Grid/Row
components.description: One grid row of body cells, in default, hover, selected, and selected-hover states.
components.details: State (default / hover / selected / selected-hover). A checkbox cell plus generic columns, built from Grid/BodyCell instances.
components.useWhen: Assembling a grid: one Row instance per record, overriding cell values.
components.dontUseWhen: A single value needs a different state — override that cell instead of adding row variants.

props.name: children
props.note: The row's BodyCells. In Figma a row is built from body cell instances.

components.name: Grid/Data grid
components.description: A generic data grid with placeholder rows, to override or rebuild for a real dataset.
components.details: Generic grid with placeholder data: two selected rows and one cell in the error state. Override values per screen.
components.useWhen: Starting a data view quickly; override headers and cell values, or rebuild rows from Grid/Row.
components.dontUseWhen: The layout isn't tabular (use cards or a list).

props.name: label
props.note: The grid's accessible name.

props.name: columns
props.note: The application owns the data: the grid shows what it is given and reports what the person asks for. In Figma, columns are edited on the instance.

props.name: rows
props.note: The application owns the data: the grid shows what it is given and reports what the person asks for. In Figma, rows are instances with overridden values.

props.name: tones
props.note: The tone of each chip label. In Figma, set on each chip.

props.name: rowKey
props.note: Which column identifies a row, for selection.

props.name: selected
props.note: The selected rows. In Figma, each row's State.

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.note: Reports selection, including select-all and Shift ranges; Figma has no behavior.

props.name: sort
props.note: The sorted column. In Figma, each header cell's Sort.

props.name: onSortChange
props.note: Reports a request to sort; Figma has no behavior.

props.name: unsortable
props.note: Columns that can't be sorted. In Figma, each header cell's Show sort.

props.name: fill
props.note: Stretches descriptive text columns to fill the container, as the plugin does when it fits a grid to a screen.

props.name: loading
props.note: Shows skeleton rows and marks the grid busy. In Figma, place Grid/Skeleton row instances under the header.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.note: What the first skeleton row and screen readers say while loading.

props.name: empty
props.note: The EmptyState shown when there are no rows. In Figma, place Grid/Empty state under the header.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.note: What screen readers hear when the empty state appears.

components.name: Grid/Pagination
components.description: Shows the visible range under a grid, with Previous and Next buttons.
components.details: Footer under the grid. Range and Page are text properties; Previous and Next are exposed Button instances, so their State (e.g. disabled on the first or last page) is set from this component's panel.
components.useWhen: A grid shows one page of a larger result set.
components.dontUseWhen: All rows fit on screen, or the list scrolls continuously — omit pagination.

props.name: onPrevious
props.note: Called for Previous; Figma has no behavior.

props.name: onNext
props.note: Called for Next; Figma has no behavior.

props.name: previousDisabled
props.note: On the first page. In Figma, set on the exposed Previous button instance (State).

props.name: nextDisabled
props.note: On the last page. In Figma, set on the exposed Next button instance (State).

components.name: Grid/Skeleton row
components.description: A placeholder row shown while grid rows load.
components.details: Loading placeholder with the grid's column widths: surface/skeleton bars, numeric bars right-aligned. Show label adds a "Loading rows…" label (Label text property) — turn it on for the first row. Mark the grid aria-busy in code.
components.useWhen: Rows are loading: stack 3–5 under the header, matching the expected row count.
components.dontUseWhen: A load takes under ~300 ms (show nothing), or the load failed or returned nothing (use Grid/Empty state).

props.name: columns
props.note: The grid's columns, one bar each. In Figma the row is drawn for the generic grid's columns.

components.name: Grid/Empty state
components.description: Takes the place of grid rows when there are no results or loading failed.
components.details: Shown in place of grid rows. Tone (neutral / critical): neutral for no results or nothing yet, critical for a load error (icon and title say so, not just color). Title and Message are text layers — override the copy; swap the icon from the instance. Show action toggles the exposed Action button (Clear filters / Retry).
components.useWhen: A grid has no rows to show — filters match nothing, nothing exists yet, or loading failed.
components.dontUseWhen: Rows are still loading (use Grid/Skeleton row), or only some rows have problems (flag those cells).

props.name: title
props.note: In Figma, a text layer to override.

props.name: message
props.note: In Figma, a text layer to override.

props.name: actionLabel
props.note: In Figma, set on the exposed Action button instance.

props.name: onAction
props.note: Called for the action; Figma has no behavior.

components.name: Grid/BulkActionBar
components.description: Shows the selection count and the actions for the selected grid rows.
components.details: Shown above a grid while rows are selected. The count is text: select-all is the checkbox in the grid's header, so the bar has no checkbox of its own. Count and Select all are text properties; Show select all hides the Select all link (e.g. once all matching rows are selected); Show destructive toggles the danger action. Hint and Show hint (off by default) explain why an action is disabled. Action buttons are exposed instances — rename them and set their state from the bar instance.
components.useWhen: One or more grid rows are selected and the actions apply to all of them.
components.dontUseWhen: Nothing is selected (hide the bar), or an action applies to a single row (put it in the row).

props.name: onSelectAll
props.note: Called for "Select all N matching"; Figma has no behavior.

props.name: hintId
props.note: Lets a disabled action point to the hint that explains it (aria-describedby).

props.name: children
props.note: The action Buttons. In Figma they are exposed button instances.

figmaOnly.reason: In code the actions are children: leave the destructive button out instead of hiding it.

components.name: Summary/Summary metric
components.description: Shows one headline number, with an optional progress bar against a target.
components.details: Label, value, and optional progress vs. target. Status (normal / over-target): over-target adds a warning icon and text in addition to the bar color. State (default / loading): loading shows a skeleton bar and "Loading…" in place of the value. Long labels truncate; the value never does — use compact notation (e.g. $12.35B) for large numbers and put the full value in Detail. Resize the Bar layer to reflect progress. Padding and the gap between its parts follow Density → card/padding and card/gap.
components.useWhen: A single headline number someone checks at a glance, optionally against a target or limit.
components.dontUseWhen: Comparing many values over time (use a chart or grid), or the number needs row-level detail.

props.name: value
props.note: In Figma, a text layer to override: it differs per variant, so it isn't a property.

props.name: detail
props.note: In Figma, a text layer to override: it differs per variant, so it isn't a property.

props.name: progress
props.note: Progress toward the target, 0 to 1. In Figma, resize the Bar layer.

components.name: Input/Text
components.description: A labeled text field with helper text and validation states.
components.details: Text input with label and helper text. State: default / hover / focus / error / error-focus / warning / warning-focus / disabled; error and warning add an icon and colored helper text, and a flagged field keeps its border when focused, with the focus ring outside it. Content: value / placeholder (Placeholder text in text/secondary). Label, Value, Placeholder, Helper, Show label, and Show helper are component properties; long values truncate. Field height follows Density → control/height.
components.useWhen: Entering free text or a number (amounts, rates, IDs).
components.dontUseWhen: The value comes from a fixed list (use a select). Hide the label (Show label off) only when a visible label sits right next to the field, and give the field an accessible name in code.

figmaOnly.reason: In code the field shows its placeholder whenever the value is empty, so there is nothing to choose.

components.name: Input/Select
components.description: A labeled dropdown for choosing one option from a short list.
components.details: Select with label and helper text. State: default / hover / focus / open (menu below the field, covering the helper) / error / error-focus / warning / warning-focus / disabled; error and warning add an icon and colored helper text, and a flagged field keeps its border when focused, with the focus ring outside it. Content: value / placeholder (Placeholder text in text/secondary). Label, Value, Placeholder, Helper, Show label, and Show helper are component properties; long values truncate. Field height follows Density → control/height.
components.useWhen: Choosing one option from a list of about 5–15 known values.
components.dontUseWhen: There are only 2–3 options (show them all) or the list is long and searchable (use a combobox). Hide the label (Show label off) only when a visible label sits right next to the field, and give the field an accessible name in code.

props.name: options
props.note: The choices. In Figma they are the Option instances inside Input/Menu.

props.name: onValueChange
props.note: Reports the option the user chose; Figma has no behavior.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.note: Reports the menu opening and closing; Figma has no behavior.

props.name: name
props.note: The field's name when it is submitted with a form.

figmaOnly.reason: In code the field shows its placeholder whenever nothing is selected, so there is nothing to choose.

components.name: Input/Option
components.description: One row in a select's open menu.
components.details: One menu row. State (default / hover / focus / selected / disabled); selected adds a check icon and bold label, and focus (the option the arrow keys are on) adds a focus ring inside the row to the hover fill. Label is a text property; long labels truncate. Height follows Density → control/height.
components.useWhen: Listing choices in Input/Menu (a select's open list).
components.dontUseWhen: The choices act immediately (use a menu of actions) or need multi-select (use checkboxes).

components.name: Input/Menu
components.description: The open list of options shown under a select.
components.details: Open list for Input/Select: a raised panel of Input/Option instances. Options are exposed instances — set each one's Label and State from this component's panel; hide extra rows to shorten the list.
components.useWhen: Showing a select's options (it's placed under the field in Input/Select State = open).
components.dontUseWhen: The list needs search or grouping beyond ~15 options (use a combobox).

components.name: Input/Option with description
components.description: A two-line menu row with a label and a muted description.
components.details: Two-line menu row: Label plus a muted Description. State (default / hover / selected / disabled); selected adds a check icon and bold label. Label and Description are text properties; both truncate.
components.useWhen: Each choice needs a short explanation — a saved view and its filters, an account and its number.
components.dontUseWhen: One line is enough (use Input/Option).

components.name: Input/Menu heading
components.description: A group heading inside a menu.
components.details: Group heading inside a menu. Label is a text property. Not interactive.
components.useWhen: A menu has two or more groups of options (e.g. predefined and saved views).
components.dontUseWhen: The menu has a single group — omit the heading.

components.name: Tabs/Tab
components.description: Switches between views of the same data, with an optional count.
components.details: View switcher above the grid. State: default / hover / focus / disabled / selected / selected-focus. Label, Count, and Show count are component properties; long labels truncate. Selected adds an underline and bold label; focus adds a focus/ring outline. A selected tab has no hover state: it is already the current view, so pointing at it changes nothing.
components.useWhen: Switching between views of the same data (e.g. All / Open / Closed).
components.dontUseWhen: Navigating between pages or steps (use navigation), or filtering by many values (use filters).

components.name: Overlay/Dialog
components.description: A modal dialog for one focused task, with a title, a body, and Cancel and primary actions.
components.details: Modal dialog: Title, Show close, a Body slot for the instance's own content, and exposed Cancel and Primary buttons (set the primary's label and disabled state from this component's panel). Raised surface with a border.
components.useWhen: Confirming or completing one focused task without leaving the screen (sign off, rename, confirm a destructive action).
components.dontUseWhen: The task needs the rest of the screen for reference (use a side panel), or it's only a message (use inline status).

props.name: open
props.note: Whether the dialog is showing. In Figma a dialog is placed on the canvas or not.

props.name: onClose
props.note: Called for Cancel, the close button, and Escape; Figma has no behavior.

props.name: cancelLabel
props.note: In Figma, set on the exposed Cancel button instance.

props.name: primaryLabel
props.note: In Figma, set on the exposed Primary button instance.

props.name: primaryKind
props.note: In Figma, set on the exposed Primary button instance (Kind).

props.name: primaryDisabled
props.note: In Figma, set on the exposed Primary button instance (State).

props.name: onPrimary
props.note: Called for the primary action; Figma has no behavior.

icons.name: Icon/*
icons.description: The "<name>" icon, a 16px outline glyph that takes its color from the component using it.
icons.details: 16px outline icon. Parent components recolor the Glyph layer; resize with icon/size or size/*.
icons.useWhen: Supporting a label, or as an instance-swap value in Button, Status badge, and similar components.
icons.dontUseWhen: It's the only way to convey meaning — pair it with text or an accessible name.

props.name: name
props.note: Which icon: the part of the Figma name after Icon/.
